subject: Site sprint checklist — constrained nodepools & eviction policy
messages:
From: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@greenfield.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Site sprint checklist — constrained nodepools & eviction policy

Hi team,

Thanks again for walking through the Greenfield constrained-site requirements this morning. Per our call, the site has the following constraints we need to bake into the preflight and the sprint: limited rack U (2x A100-equivalent), single upstream L3 egress, and a strict local-disk quota (no more than 1.2TB per host available to K8s).

Questions and asks before Monday's kickoff: 
- Can Redwood provide a concrete nodefleet sizing recommendation for a 3-node control/3-node worker mini-cluster with mixed GPU/CPU pools?
- We need an eviction & PVC fallback policy that preserves model weight caches but evicts low-priority batch pods first — will that require custom CSI or annotations?
- Please confirm which telemetry is safe to route off-site (we can only permit anonymized metrics through the VPC egress).

I've attached an inventory CSV and uploaded a short site photo deck to the shared Drive link. If you can reply with a one-page checklist and a short decision matrix for nodepool sizing, we'll include it in the kickoff packet.

Thanks,
Maria Ortega
DevOps Lead, Greenfield Systems
(mobile) +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: site-inventory-20261012.csv (CSV), site-photos.zip (reference)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@greenfield.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Site sprint checklist — constrained nodepools & eviction policy

Maria — thanks for the clear inventory. First-pass answers inline and next steps below.

1) Nodefleet sizing (recommendation):
- Control plane: 3 x m5.large-like CPU-only nodes (small footprint, HA control plane).
- Workers: 3-node worker pool distributed across racks: 1 GPU-heavy (1x A100 equiv + 256GB RAM), 2 CPU-heavy (128–192GB RAM) to host inference API + batch. Given the 1.2TB host limit, plan for local NVMe for model cache (500–700GB per GPU host) and hostPath CSI for cache eviction.

2) Eviction & PVC fallback:
- Primary: use immediate-local PVCs for model cache with annotation to prefer deletion of batch-cache volumes.
- Fallback: persistent hostPath-backed PVC class (non-replicated) that the runtime treats as lower-priority.
- We recommend a small mutating webhook that sets pod priorityClass and PVC class based on labels (no custom CSI required initially). If Greenfield needs cross-host PVC migration, we can discuss a CSI rewrite later.

3) Telemetry flow:
- Allowed: anonymized usage counters, aggregated latency P50/P95. Disallowed: raw prompt texts, full trace payloads. We will provide a telemetry filter sidecar (policy config) to run inside the VPC.

Next steps (ask to internal team): Marissa/Laura/Logan — can you validate the worker sizing above against the inventory baseline and produce a 1-page decision matrix (target: 1x PDF)? Also flag any storage classes we should pre-provision.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up after you respond.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — I reviewed the inventory quickly. A few clarifications and an initial checklist attached (eviction-policy-draft.md):
- Storage classes: we have to avoid dynamic EBS-like provisioning. Recommend two classes: fast-local (hostPath-backed, pre-paved NVMe) and durable-cluster (NFS/SMB over on-site NAS for model artifacts).
- Pod priorities: set inference svc = high, realtime-rt = medium, batch = low. We'll add tolerations to ensure batch goes to non-GPU nodes.
- OOM/eviction guardrails: kube-reserved & system-reserved must be strict on GPU hosts — set kube-reserved.cpu=1000m and memory=8Gi to protect model-serving processes.

I've attached an eviction-policy-draft.md with specific priorityClass YAML and a short decision matrix (one table). Priyom — can you validate whether the hostPath class will fit with the node lifecycle automation you're designing?

Marissa
Sr. PM, Infra Delivery

Attachments: eviction-policy-draft.md

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Site sprint checklist — constrained nodepools & eviction policy

Quick confirmation from infra automation: hostPath-backed 'fast-local' class is OK for cache-only volumes if we treat them as ephemeral in our node-replacement workflows. A couple implementation notes: 
- Node replacement: drain -> cordon -> replace NVMe -> rejoin; make sure controller for model cache can warm the cache on boot using a prefetch job (we'll provide a sample prefetcher).
- PVC binding: set volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer so PVCs bind to the correct node type.
- Monitoring: add kubelet volume stats exporter so we can alert when free local bytes < 15% and trigger scheduled cache eviction.

I'll drop the sample prefetch job and a node lifecycle playbook in the shared Drive link by EOD.

— Priyom
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
